title: `st.bar_chart` should not be zoomable
body: # Summary The bar chart zooms, which I can't think of a scenario for. # Steps to reproduce ```py import streamlit as st import pandas as pd import numpy as np st.title('Uber pickups in NYC') DATE_COLUMN = 'date/time' DATA_URL = ('https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/' 'streamlit-demo-data/uber-raw-data-sep14.csv.gz') [USER].cache def load_data(nrows): data = pd.read_csv(DATA_URL, nrows=nrows) lowercase = lambda x: str(x).lower() data.rename(lowercase, axis='columns', inplace=True) data[DATE_COLUMN] = pd.to_datetime(data[DATE_COLUMN]) return data data_load_state = st.text('Loading data...') data = load_data(10000) data_load_state.text("Done! (using st.cache)") if st.checkbox('Show raw data'): st.subheader('Raw data') st.write(data) st.subheader('Number of pickups by hour') hist_values = np.histogram(data[DATE_COLUMN].dt.hour, bins=24, range=(0,24))[0] st.bar_chart(hist_values) ``` ## Expected behavior: Not sure. Maybe no zoom. ## Actual behavior: # Debug info - Streamlit version: 0.65.2 --- Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users. **If you'd like the Streamlit team to prioritize this feature request, please use the 👍 (thumbs up emoji) reaction in response to the initial post.**

comments.body:
~Hm, I can't seem to reproduce this (at least, not on the latest version of Streamlit, Windows, Chrome). Using your exact code snippet gives me:~

![](https://i.imgur.com/P0EbuM1.png)

Though, it is kind of weird that the lines on the bar chart are so thin -- not sure if that's a bug with barchart or working as intended.

Oh, silly me, I thought you were saying that it was zoomed out by default, but you meant that "Barcharts should not zoom at all"; and my gut instinct is that you're absolutely right, there's no reason for that to exist.

It might make sense to zoom horizontally only. The vertical zoom for a bar chart is odd. You can constrain the interactions to horizontal like this: ``` scales = alt.selection_interval(bind="scales", encodings=["x"]) st.write(alt.Chart(df).mark_bar().encode( alt.Y("count()"), alt.X("Body Mass (g)", bin=True) ).add_selection(scales)) ``` I think this interaction can be useful if there are a lot of bars.

[USER] -- just saw your comment, and agree that horizontal zooming seems like a better fit than vertical zooming for bar charts. But the code snippet you provided doesn't seem to interact well with the ordinal scale on x-axis... 

Am I invoking the altair library incorrectly somehow? (And/or: any chance of setting this default behavior in the upstream altair library, rather than hacking it in st.bar_chart =3)

```
import streamlit as st
import altair as alt
import pandas as pd


df = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "index": [3, 4, 5, 6],
        "numbers": [10, 50, 30, 40],
    }
)
st.write(df)

st.write("Zooms horizontally")
scales = alt.selection_interval(bind="scales", encodings=["x"])
st.write(
    alt.Chart(df)
    .mark_bar()
    .encode(alt.Y("numbers"), alt.X("index"))
    .add_selection(scales)
)

st.write("Zooms vertically")
st.write(
    alt.Chart(df)
    .mark_bar()
    .encode(
        alt.Y("numbers"),
        alt.X("index", type="ordinal"),
    )
    .add_selection(scales)
    .interactive()
)
```

> But the code snippet you provided doesn't seem to interact well with the ordinal scale on x-axis...

Can you send a gif of what you are seeing?

> Can you send a gif of what you are seeing?

How about an S4A app :wink:? https://share.streamlit.io/akrolsmir/guac-bottle/barchart-zoom

![streamlit-streamlit_app-2020-10-22-12-10-66](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/856034/96937913-11ae4300-147e-11eb-8e72-af1eacbcae28.gif)

Perfect. 

```
st.write("Zooms vertically")
st.write(
    alt.Chart(df)
    .mark_bar()
    .encode(
        alt.Y("numbers"),
        alt.X("index", type="ordinal"),
    )
    .add_selection(scales)
    .interactive()
)
```

I would only do one: set the selection or call `.interactive`.

And yes, I think the defaults in Altair could be better.

> I would only do one: set the selection or call `.interactive`.

Hm, the problem I'm seeing is: For X type=ordinal with only the selection set, the graph doesn't scroll at all; with only `.interactive` set, the graph zooms vertically. I couldn't figure out how to get it to scroll horizontally with type=ordinal.
It zooms horizontally in your gif. I'm missing something.

> It zooms horizontally in your gif. I'm missing something.

Ah, sorry if that wasn't clear. In the gif, the first graph does NOT have "type=ordinal" set; that is, the only way I could get horizontal scrolling to work was by removing "type=ordinal". 

But this is not super desirable for the graph otherwise; you'll notice that the bars in the first chart are thin, and the number line extends in both direction (whereas a bar chart should only have the ordinal buckets for that the data fits into?)
I see. Zooming in a categorical chart probably isn't all that useful anyway so you could probably disable interactions completely.

I've found functionality in horizontal zooming. I have a dataset with very large and very small values, it's important that I can display both the high values and zoom in on areas with the smaller values.
I see. In that case you would want only horizontal zooming, though. I see why that could be useful.
Given that there aren't any upvotes on this request, I'm going to close the issue. Happy to reopen if something changes.
Hmm, I think it's problematic to support zooming on bar charts and the discussion shows that it's a problem people agree with.
This was closed as completed, and yet my bar charts still zoom, breaking scrolling behavior. Please either disable zooming entirely or provide a way to disable it from the st.bar_chart function.
